items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Because the people that heard him a lot, Teagarden told me this, said that there was never any experience that he ever had in music like hearing Beiderbecke play live.

ctx.x: But if you’d like to ask me what else I would like to do, that I’ve fantasized about, you know there are all kinds of things with Beiderbecke that I’ve fantasized about. Beiderbecke died in Queens and he died a tragic, down and out situation you know. His last year he was just around and Teagarden said that in the recording studio they would try to record and he overheard him, kind of eerie, talk to the cornet and say, “Don’t let me down, don’t let me down today” you know. And this guy, he started having trouble…

Because the people that heard him a lot, Teagarden told me this, said that there was never any experience that he ever had in music like hearing Beiderbecke play live. It was — the records never quite got it. And there was never anything like it. Teagarden said, “I think he was the greatest artist that there ever was in history.” Teagarden was such a nut about Beiderbecke. He was just a — and Teagarden was a great admirer of many other players too, and particularly Armstrong. He had heard Armstrong when he was a…
And it’s amazing that at the same time he was doing that he was writing some of those piano pieces that he did too.
